claims.text: An AlTiCrZrNbTa coating containing about 10 at.% Al will form a continuous composite oxide layer during high-temperature steam oxidation.
The composite oxide layer will consist mainly of Al2O3, TiO2, and Cr2O3.
The composite oxide will suppress oxygen diffusion and maintain coating adhesion more effectively than coatings with zero or excessive Al.
The Zircaloy-4 substrate composition is Zr-98.2%, Sn-1.5%, Fe-0.2%, and Cr-0.1%.
The sputtered AlTiCrZrNbTa films are initially dense, defect-free, amorphous, and approximately 4 micrometers thick.
DC magnetron sputtering can produce a coating targeted at about 10 at.% Al, with measured values near 11 at.%, while maintaining a thickness near 4 micrometers.
The proposed performance regime is flowing steam generated from ultrapure water at 0.2 mL/min, at 1000 degrees Celsius for 60 minutes, with optional evaluation at 1100 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes.
A dense and adherent Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 layer will minimize oxygen penetration and maintain interface adhesion.
At about 10 at.% Al, favorable thermodynamics promote early nucleation of protective Al2O3 and TiO2.
At about 10 at.% Al, chromium is driven outward and stabilizes Cr2O3.
The resulting composite oxide layer acts as an effective oxygen barrier.
An Al-free coating produces fragmented and delaminated oxide scales.
Coatings containing at least 17 at.% Al tend to form deleterious Al-Ti or Al-Zr intermetallics.
Al-Ti or Al-Zr intermetallics formed at high Al content disrupt oxide continuity.
A coating containing about 10 at.% Al will have a lower oxidation rate than Al-free, below-5-at.% Al, and at-least-17-at.% Al coatings.
A coating containing about 10 at.% Al will exhibit reduced oxygen uptake relative to the stated lower- and higher-Al baselines.
A coating containing about 10 at.% Al will show less fragmentation and delamination than the stated lower- and higher-Al baselines.
The hypothesis is not established for longer exposures, different temperatures, or different steam flow rates.
Small variations in actual aluminum content may affect oxidation performance.

Failure of the approximately 10 at.% Al coating to outperform both Al-free and high-Al controls in oxidation rate, oxide continuity, and adhesion under identical conditions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline is called an 'Al-free (0 at.% Al) AlTiCrZrNbTa coating,' even though the formula AlTiCrZrNbTa explicitly denotes an Al-containing composition.
